problem: Existing VLM-based socially compliant navigation methods assume a single ground-truth action per scene, penalizing equally valid alternatives, and rely on large, slow VLMs. Existing datasets like SNEI are small and give only one action per scenario.
motivation: Social norms are ambiguous and several actions (e.g. stop or bypass) can be equally acceptable, so a single-label formulation limits real-world handling of social uncertainty. Real-time deployment also needs low-latency small models, which have not been explored for social navigation.
key_idea: Fine-tune a small VLM (NVILA-Lite-2B) to output a ranked set of multiple acceptable discrete actions, using a meta-cognitive system prompt (self-evaluation plus competitor-stimulated reasoning) to boost reasoning.
insight: The MCP system prompt helps the small model more than explicit CoT-style causal reasoning turns, which gave no consistent gain (Pred@n 0.351 vs 0.389 without). In the ablation, single MCP components give inconsistent gains, and only self-evaluation combined with the AI-competitor prompt gives the best results across all metrics (APG 0.595 vs 0.532 baseline). MCP mainly helps on Medium and Difficult scenes (Difficult APG 0.286 vs 0.143), while Easy scenes are already saturated. Caveat: the test set is only 79 samples, so differences are noisy.
method: Multi-action ranking formulation: supervise the VLM to generate a ranked subset of six discrete actions (forward, forward-left, forward-right, turn left, turn right, stop) via autoregressive next-token loss; ordering is learned through token dependency.
Meta-cognitive self-evaluation prompt: a system prompt asking for a silent recursive draft-score-refine loop with a 90-point threshold (scores above 100 allowed) and output of the final answer only.

Competitor-stimulated reasoning prompt: a role prompt telling the model to compete against humans, other AI models, or itself; the best variant is the AI competitor. Concatenated with the self-evaluation prompt to form S_MCP.

Curated multi-action dataset: 789 samples (710 train / 79 test), each a three-turn dialogue (scene observation, motion prediction, ranked actions), annotated by two humans using a Feasibility -> Social norms -> Efficiency hierarchy.
Five metrics: Pred@1, Pred@n, APG (all predictions inside the GT set), MAA (rank-weighted accuracy with weights 6..1), and ER (hallucinated action rate).
Training: NVILA-Lite-2B, vision projector plus LoRA fine-tuning, lr 1e-4, global batch 64, 10 epochs, DeepSpeed ZeRO-2, BF16, on 4 RTX 8000 GPUs.

setting.training_data: 710 self-curated multi-action social navigation samples (re-annotated, SNEI-style, three-turn dialogues, dual human annotators)
setting.observation: single monocular RGB scene image plus multi-turn text dialogue
setting.action_space: six discrete high-level motion primitives (forward, forward-left, forward-right, turn left, turn right, stop), output as a ranked set

numbers.eval_set_note: 79 held-out test samples from the authors' 789-sample dataset
numbers.evidence: Table 2 comparison with zero-shot large multimodal models; Table 1 main results
Table 1: Comparison with and without MCP, and with causal reasoning

numbers.extra: extra CoT-style reasoning turn, no system prompt

numbers_note: Only results on the authors' own dataset; no standard navigation benchmark. FPS is given only for the comparison table.
results: On the 79-sample test set, MAction-SocialNav with MCP reaches Pred@1 0.760, APG 0.595 and ER 0.264, versus zero-shot Claude (0.570 / 0.025 / 0.668) and GPT-4o (0.405 / 0.000 / 0.642). It runs at 1.524 FPS versus 0.452 for Claude and 0.314 for GPT-4o. MCP improves over the no-MCP variant (APG 0.532) and over causal reasoning.
limitations: Small dataset (789 samples, 79 test) and evaluation is offline on images, with no closed-loop or real-robot test.
Coarse six-action discrete space needs a separate local planner; safety and efficiency metrics such as collision rate are not evaluated.
Zero-shot baselines are only GPT-4o and Claude, with no fine-tuned VLM baseline (e.g. Social-LLaVA); the ablation on the MCP variants is noisy.
